title: Unit equation for a normalized rational Verdier scalar comparison
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$, a prime $\ell\ne D.p$, and a separated finite-type $D.k$-scheme $X$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Use the raw rational constructible categories and canonical coefficient functors [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and the normalized rational Verdier data and comparison predicate [def-sf-rational-verdier-data]. Let $E$ be finite over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, $w_E$ a coherent integral dualizing datum [def-sf-coherent-integral-dualizing-datum], $A$ a rational Verdier datum, and $e$ any comparison for the identity embedding satisfying ExtensionProperties. There is a natural isomorphism $j:T_{E/E}\cong\mathrm{id}$ whose component on every integral representative is the localization of the canonical integral multiplication unit [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension]. For every rational $K$, $e.\mathrm{comparison}_K=j_{A.DK}\,A.D(j_K)$, with left-to-right categorical composition. No coefficient-field family or nonidentity composition equation is asserted.

proof.text: The completion comparison is a natural transformation, invertible on constructible complete inputs. Its inverse naturality, followed by the ordinary tensor identity natural isomorphism, makes the specified integral multiplication units a natural isomorphism on the constructible subcategory. The pure-tensor map formula at coefficient one identifies rational scalar extension precomposed with localization with integral scalar extension followed by localization. Descend the localized integral unit using naturalIso_of_integral to obtain j; its component equation gives precisely the required HEq normalization.

Apply evaluation_naturality to A.ordinary, then specialize comparison_cocycles to the identity field embedding and identical dualizing data and presentations. Its third identity equation gives beta_K followed by D(unit_K inverse)=unit_DK. Postcompose with D(unit_K hom); functoriality and the inverse identities cancel the inverse-unit factor. Restrict this equality to the integral constructible category and apply localization.

For any rational object K, use its literal integral representative K.obj. ExtensionProperties identifies the localized beta with e.comparison. The normalized component of j at the integral dual, together with A.objects, identifies the first factor. A.pure at coefficient one identifies the second factor with A.dual(j_K). The object formulas for scalar extension and duality fix the three endpoints, so heterogeneous composition and the localized integral equality prove the desired equation. No faithfulness, lattice choices, nonzero-object condition or extra geometry is used.

theorem extension_unit
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    (wE : IntegralFiniteExtension.DualizingDatum l X D hl E)
    (A : Datum D l hl X E wE)
    (e : Extension D l hl X E E (AlgHom.id (Padic l) E) wE wE A A)
    (he : ExtensionProperties D l hl X E E (AlgHom.id (Padic l) E) wE wE A A e) :
    ∃ j : scalar l X E E (AlgHom.id (Padic l) E) ≅ 𝟭 (sfRationalConstructibleCategory l E X),
      (∀ K : sfIntegralConstructibleCategory l E X,
        HEq (j.hom.app ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l E X).obj K))
          ((sfRationalConstructibleLocalization l E X).map
            (ObjectProperty.homMk
              (X := (integralScalar l X E E (AlgHom.id (Padic l) E)).obj K) (Y := K)
              (IntegralFiniteExtension.unit l E X K.obj K.property.1).hom))) ∧
      ∀ K : sfRationalConstructibleCategory l E X,
        e.comparison.hom.app (op K) =
          j.hom.app (A.dual.obj (op K)) ≫
            A.dual.map (j.hom.app K).op
